description: Overlap between CISA ScubaGear policies and Prowler Microsoft 365 checks, used by scripts/build-prowler-cases.py to compare the two oracles. Policies and checks were paired by reading both rule sets; ids are exact. Rows that share a ScubaGear policy are conjunctive parts: the policy counts as met only when every row passes. Rows with a null scubagear_policy are Prowler checks with no ScubaGear counterpart (Google Workspace excluded).

confidence.exact: Both engines test the same setting with the same pass condition; edge handling (exclusions, licence gating) may still differ and is in the note.
confidence.partial: The engines test overlapping but different conditions (other thresholds, a subset of the settings or another evidence source), so a disagreement is expected and is not by itself evidence of a wrong label.

rows.note: Same control: an enabled all-users, all-apps Conditional Access policy for other and exchangeActiveSync clients with a block grant. ScubaGear also rejects excluded roles and unconfigured exclusions.
Both target high user risk. Prowler accepts a password change plus MFA grant; ScubaGear requires a block grant and an AAD P2 plan.
Both block risky sign-ins through Conditional Access. Prowler needs high and medium risk and no excluded apps; ScubaGear needs high risk only plus an AAD P2 plan.
Both want MFA for all users and apps. Prowler reads only the mfa built-in control; ScubaGear also accepts authentication strengths and rejects excluded roles.

Both need Authenticator to show app name and location. Prowler fails when Authenticator is disabled; ScubaGear treats that, or enforced phishing-resistant MFA, as not applicable and also checks targets and software OATH.
Covers Sms and Voice only; ScubaGear needs Sms, Voice and Email all disabled, so the verdict combines this row with the Email row.
Covers Email only; the policy is met only when this row and the Sms and Voice row both pass.

Both want phishing-resistant MFA for administrator roles. Prowler matches the built-in strength name, treats a policy with no included roles as an administrator policy and returns MANUAL for custom strengths; ScubaGear needs every privileged role included and no excluded roles.
Both require a managed device. Prowler needs domainJoinedDevice with mfa and an OR operator; ScubaGear needs exactly compliantDevice and domainJoinedDevice with OR.
Both scope a policy to security-info registration. Prowler needs domainJoinedDevice with mfa and OR; ScubaGear accepts compliantDevice or domainJoinedDevice.
Same control: an enabled all-users, all-apps policy for the device code flow transfer method with a block grant. ScubaGear also rejects excluded roles and unconfigured exclusions.
Same setting: authorization policy defaultUserRolePermissions.allowedToCreateApps must be false.

Both restrict user consent. Prowler passes only when no ManagePermissionGrantsForSelf policy is assigned; ScubaGear fails the Microsoft-managed option and tolerates the low-risk option when no risky permissions are classified.
Both want the admin consent workflow on. Prowler reads the admin consent request policy; ScubaGear reads the EnableAdminConsentRequests directory setting, which the builder maps across.
Prowler needs four restrictions not disabled (password addition, password lifetime, custom password, certificate lifetime); ScubaGear 5.5 tests password addition only, enabled for all apps.
Prowler ignores the lifetime value and date scope; ScubaGear 5.6 needs a password lifetime of 180 days or less for all apps and is not applicable when 5.5 passes.
Prowler ignores the lifetime value and date scope; ScubaGear 5.7 needs a certificate lifetime of 365 days or less for all apps.
Both test password expiry. Prowler reads the first domain and passes only on 2147483647; ScubaGear checks every verified managed root domain and also accepts null.
Same control with different bounds: Prowler allows two to four Global Administrators, ScubaGear two to eight.
Same control: privileged users must not be synced from on-premises. The role sets differ slightly because Prowler uses its own administrator role list.
Both want approval to activate Global Administrator. Prowler also needs approvers configured; ScubaGear also needs an AAD P2 plan.
Same setting: guestUserRoleId must be the limited or restricted guest role.
Prowler passes adminsAndGuestInviters and none; ScubaGear requires adminsAndGuestInviters exactly.

Same intent, different object: Prowler reads outbound spam policies (AutoForwardingMode), ScubaGear reads remote domains with AutoForwardEnabled. The kit exports no outbound spam policy, so every case is UNMAPPED (not_exported).
Both need DKIM signing enabled per domain, but ScubaGear also requires a published DKIM DNS record and takes its domain list from the SPF records, while Prowler reads the signing configurations only.
Prowler also requires an enforcing p=quarantine or p=reject policy; ScubaGear 4.1 needs only a published v=DMARC1 record.
Prowler accepts p=quarantine as well as p=reject; ScubaGear 4.2 requires p=reject.
Same setting: SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled in the Exchange Online transport configuration.

Both limit calendar sharing outside the tenant. Prowler reads the organisation sharing policy's Enabled flag; ScubaGear reads sharing policies for the all-domains wildcard. The kit exports no Enabled flag, so every case is UNMAPPED (not_exported).

Both want external senders flagged. Prowler checks native external tagging (Get-ExternalInOutlook); ScubaGear checks for an enforced transport rule that prepends the subject of NotInOrganization mail. The kit exports no external tag setting, so every case is UNMAPPED (not_exported).
Same setting: organisation AuditDisabled must be false.

Both need the common attachment filter on with the baseline's extensions. Prowler normally requires 53 recommended extensions; the run sets its recommended_blocked_file_types to exe, cmd and vbe so the check tests the same list. Prowler judges the default policy and rule-scoped custom policies and skips preset policies; ScubaGear takes the highest-priority active policy for all recipients, presets first.
Necessary part of 1.1: the common attachment filter must be on in the policies Prowler judges. It does not test the extension list, so it never overrules the comprehensive check.

Both test Safe Attachments handling of unknown malware. Prowler passes the built-in policy unconditionally, judges every custom policy that has a rule (enabled, Block and the admin-only quarantine tag) and ignores presets; ScubaGear accepts Block or DynamicDelivery on the highest-priority active policy for all recipients, presets first.
Both cover Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams. Prowler also requires Safe Documents and click-through blocked.
Prowler bundles safety tips with spoof intelligence, DMARC honouring and quarantine settings; ScubaGear 2.4 tests user warnings only.
Same setting: UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled.

Both fail a policy with AllowedSenderDomains, but Prowler judges the default and rule-scoped custom policies and skips presets, while ScubaGear's pass condition is the precedence cascade of strict preset, standard preset, custom and default policy.

Prowler requires a full set of Safe Links settings in every custom policy that has a rule, whether or not it applies; ScubaGear 7.1 tests URL comparison with the block list in the policy that applies to all recipients, presets first.

Prowler requires a full set of Safe Links settings in every custom policy that has a rule, whether or not it applies; ScubaGear 7.2 tests direct download link scanning in the policy that applies to all recipients, presets first.

Prowler requires a full set of Safe Links settings in every custom policy that has a rule, whether or not it applies; ScubaGear 7.3 tests user click tracking in the policy that applies to all recipients, presets first.
Same control: the connection filter IP allow list must be empty.
Same control: the connection filter safe list must be off.
Prowler also accepts New and existing guests; ScubaGear allows only Existing guests or Only people in your organization.
Prowler accepts an allow list or a block list; ScubaGear 1.3 requires the allow-list mode and is not applicable when sharing is off.
Same setting, different scope: ScubaGear fails if any meeting policy allows external control; Prowler reads only the Global meeting policy.
Same setting, different scope: ScubaGear fails if any meeting policy lets anonymous users start meetings; Prowler reads only the Global meeting policy.

ScubaGear 1.3 needs auto-admit other than Everyone and dial-in lobby bypass off; Prowler checks only who may bypass the lobby and passes only EveryoneInCompanyExcludingGuests, OrganizerOnly and InvitedUsers, so the fixtures' EveryoneInCompany fails it.
Same setting, different scope: ScubaGear fails if any meeting policy lets dial-in users bypass the lobby; Prowler reads only the Global meeting policy.
Same setting: AllowCloudRecording must be false in the meeting policy.
Prowler passes only when external access is off; ScubaGear also accepts external access with an allowed-domains list.
Prowler checks AllowTeamsConsumerInbound alone; ScubaGear fails only when both AllowTeamsConsumerInbound and AllowTeamsConsumer are on.
Same setting: AllowTeamsConsumer must be false; ScubaGear treats US Government tenant regions as not applicable.
Same setting: AllowEmailIntoChannel must be false.
